analysis:
The PR adds require_supported_macos() to scripts/install.sh (new function near line 412, called after select_provider_identity at about line 557). A fresh install on a known macOS version below 27 now exits 1. The function returns 0 and continues when the major version is non-numeric or unknown. It also continues, with an upgrade notice, if $BIN_DIR/$CLI_NAME or $PROVIDER_CONFIG already exists. The docs (installation.md step 1 and prerequisites, quickstart.md intro) are updated to match, with date bumps.

Security assessment: this is a client-side onboarding gate, not an authorization control. The existence check is trivially satisfiable (touch a config file), and unknown versions pass. Real serving authorization stays on the coordinator side (TB-011 App Attest, T-052/T-053/T-054 and the TB-002 routing gates). The docs state that setup choice grants no serving authorization and that the frozen legacy cohort is unchanged, so no threat assumption is invalidated. No new network, crypto or file-write surface is added. The installer still verifies bundle_hash, binary_hash, metallib_hash and the codesign designated requirement as before. Failure output goes to stderr and uses only the local sw_vers value and constants.

Not verifiable from the supplied excerpts: whether MACOS, BIN_DIR, CLI_NAME, PROVIDER_CONFIG and PROVIDER_LABEL are all defined before the call (an unset variable under set -u could abort). Also, the platform repo's embedded coordinator/api/install.sh copy must be regenerated via scripts/sync-install-embed.sh, otherwise the served installer drifts from this one. That belongs to the platform repo and is outside this PR's visible scope. installation.md has a pre-existing truncated section 1 code block, which is not new. No findings.
